Relevant files:

- src/android/androidNavigationTypes.ts — artifact/type contract conventions (ARTIFACT_KIND, SCHEMA_VERSION, FILENAME constants; nested evidence-kind unions; summary object) to mirror in the new androidComposeTypes.ts

- src/indexing/managedArtifacts.ts — single owner of the managed-artifact filename registry; new ANDROID_COMPOSE_SEMANTIC_FILENAME constant belongs in OPTIONAL_INDEX_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES

- src/indexing/runIndexCommand.ts — single owner of orchestration order, analyzer-status assembly (`replaceAnalyzerStatuses`), and the `finishIndexBuild()` function where a 7th Android builder call and analyzer-status function must be added alongside the existing six
- src/indexing/refreshIndexOutput.ts — single owner of stale-artifact cleanup; requires no code change, only correct registration in managedArtifacts.ts
- src/indexing/cacheMetadata.ts, src/indexing/partialRebuild.ts — incremental-eligibility gate; confirmed keyed off symbol-index.json schema/content only, not per-analyzer fingerprints
- src/languages/kotlin/adapter.ts — read-only precedent for existing conservative top-level-only Kotlin scanning conventions (brace-depth counter, comment/string stripping); MUST NOT be modified per fixed constraint
- src/graph-diff/types.ts — confirms no Android artifact (including android-navigation) currently participates in graph-diff; android-compose-semantic must not add a diff section in Batch 1

Upstream dependencies:
- The new analyzer depends on `roledSymbolIndex` (the fully role-enriched symbol index built earlier in finishIndexBuild()) for its Kotlin file list, exactly as buildComposeNavigationRoutes.ts already does for Compose route scanning
- Depends on `androidResult.artifact.detected` the same way android-navigation's Compose-route portion is only meaningful when an Android project was detected (though, per the fixed local-composable definitions in the external contract, Batch 1 should scan any indexed Kotlin file regardless of Android-project detection status, since Compose can theoretically appear without a fully detected Android project — this must be explicitly decided in pseudocode-packet, flagged here as a gap)

Downstream consumers: none in Batch 1 (no command, graph, or retrieval surface consumes this artifact yet; Batches 4-5 are the first consumers per the fixed roadmap)

Existing patterns to preserve:
- Analyzer-registry pattern (one `IndexAnalyzerStatus` per artifact, merged via `replaceAnalyzerStatuses`) rather than a new top-level manifest field
- Conservative/never-invent-facts failure mode: degrade to a warning or omission, never fabricate a declaration or relationship
- Optional-artifact-omitted-when-not-detected convention (`artifact.detected ? artifact : null` at the writeIndexArtifacts call site)
- Deterministic, content-derived IDs sorted before serialization (`sortById` pattern)
- Blanket stale-cleanup via managed-filename-list membership (no artifact-specific cleanup code)

Likely files or modules involved:
New: src/android/androidComposeTypes.ts, src/android/buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts (or equivalently named analyzer file).
Modified: src/android/index.ts, src/indexing/managedArtifacts.ts, src/indexing/writeIndexManifest.ts, src/indexing/runIndexCommand.ts. src/indexing/manifestTypes.ts modification is NOT expected to be required (the analyzer-registry pattern avoids a manifest schema change, exactly as android-navigation's addition required none) but is not fully ruled out until pseudocode/implementation confirms IndexSemanticArtifacts / IndexAnalyzerStatus types need no new fields.

Context gaps or uncertainty:
- Whether Compose scanning should run only when `androidResult.artifact.detected === true` (mirroring android-components' full-skip-when-no-Android-project convention) or unconditionally over all indexed Kotlin files regardless of Android-project detection (a bare Kotlin+Compose-Multiplatform-for-Desktop project, for instance, would have Compose without Android manifest/gradle evidence). This is a scope decision for pseudocode-packet, not an architecture-ownership question — flagging it here so it is not silently decided during implementation.
- Same-file duplicate-declaration-name ID tie-breaking convention (see retrieval report) — resolved in pseudocode-packet.
